title: Beyond the 956: Tony Butala, founding lead singer of The Lettermen, dies at 87
excerpt: Tony Butala, a founding member and longtime lead singer of the 1960s pop vocal group The Lettermen, has died at 87. The group announced his death on November 1, 2026.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Tony Butala, a founding member and longtime lead singer of the 1960s pop vocal group The Lettermen, has died at 87.

Butala passed away on November 1, 2026, according to an announcement on the group's Facebook page. No cause of death has been publicly disclosed.

Born November 20, 1938, in Sharon, Pennsylvania, Butala began singing professionally as a child, performing on a Pittsburgh radio show at age 8. He later moved to Hollywood, where he sang with the Robert Mitchell Boys Choir and provided the singing voice for Slightly in Disney's Peter Pan.

In 1958, he helped form The Lettermen, which became known for its signature three-part harmonies. The group scored a Top 20 hit with "The Way You Look Tonight" in 1961 and went on to earn 11 gold records and four Grammy nominations. In 2020, The Lettermen received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Butala led the group until his retirement in 2019, and he was the last surviving member of the original trio.

"Tony never met a stranger. His life was a living example of talent, perseverance, and refinement," the group's statement read. "But above all, his true joy was entertaining and sharing his music with audiences worldwide. His spirit will live on with every Lettermen performance."

Rest in Peace, Tony Butala.

Sources: The Lettermen announcement on Facebook, via Parade; WKBN.
